title: Prevent traceback when KeyboardInterrupt occurs during CLI exit or abort
answers: Why does pressing Ctrl-C during error reporting show a traceback in Click?
How to prevent a late KeyboardInterrupt from crashing Command.main?
Why does a second Ctrl-C escape Command.main instead of exiting cleanly?
body:
Symptom: Pressing Ctrl-C while a command is aborting, reporting an error, or exiting crashes with an unhandled KeyboardInterrupt traceback instead of exiting cleanly.
Root cause: src/click/core.py:Command.main executed message display (such as e.show()) and sys.exit() directly inside except blocks unprotected by interrupt handling.
Fix pattern: Collect error presentation callbacks and target exit codes inside inner handlers, defer execution to a teardown block, and wrap teardown in an outer interrupt handler that preserves the exit code.
Constraints: Applies to standalone CLI execution; non-standalone mode (standalone_mode=False) must propagate interrupts and exceptions to the caller.
applies: CLI execution and interrupt handling in src/click/core.py:Command.main
says: Pressing cancel while an error message prints displays an ugly crash stack trace.
Hitting interrupt a second time during command shutdown should still exit cleanly without tracebacks.
Raw crash output appears in terminal when cancelling a command that is already failing.
Ensure aborting during error reporting terminates cleanly without dumping internal program errors.
Terminal prints an unhandled crash traceback if cancelled while the tool is exiting.
